title: Validate and protect every version snapshot operation
description:
Audit key: S07
Evidence class: source-risk
Baseline: f6ca003f255fe7636e97d63ba80e4bfcd9cffa32 (2026-09-30 Australia/Sydney)
Sources: internal/version/version.go:Capture/List/Verify/Remove/Mount/manifestFilePath

Evidence:
Capture uses dest+.tmp, removes it preemptively and removes the destination before rename; Verify joins a caller label without the Capture label validator. Manifest path checking is lexical. Public package coverage is 44.2%.

Scope: Test/fix/optimise existing behaviour only. Record reproduction, changed paths, tests, measurements and commit in notes; maintain CHANGELOG.md. Unproven candidates can be resolved with a documented measurement-based no-change decision.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise invalid labels, symlinked artifacts/manifest paths, simultaneous captures, overwrite failure, missing/extra/tampered files and read-only destinations. Reuse one label/path policy; preserve the last verified snapshot on failure and keep mounted navigation correct.
notes:

Read/list/removal confinement is being fixed and qualified; Capture/Mount and overwrite recovery remain unfinished.

title: Make document conversion recoverable across partial filesystem failures
description:
Audit key: S06
Evidence class: source-risk
Baseline: f6ca003f255fe7636e97d63ba80e4bfcd9cffa32 (2026-09-30 Australia/Sydney)
Sources: internal/projectconvert/convert.go:Run; internal/translate/conversion.go

Evidence:
Run claims atomic conversion but sequentially renames every target, then deletes sources, then saves changed configuration. A later rename/delete/config failure leaves earlier changes in place. Temporary names are predictable target+.tmp.

Scope: Test/fix/optimise existing behaviour only. Record reproduction, changed paths, tests, measurements and commit in notes; maintain CHANGELOG.md. Unproven candidates can be resolved with a documented measurement-based no-change decision.
acceptance_criteria: Inject target write/rename, source deletion and config/state-save failures. Preserve originals and translation state or perform verified rollback; reject target collisions and existing temporary symlinks. Successful Markdown/MPD conversions remain semantically equivalent.
notes:
2026-10-02 confirmed authenticated conversion data loss at e8eac75:3 unsafe source/state boundaries accepted, external state-parent JSON overwritten and targets published; predictable index.mpd.tmp consumes an unrelated owned file and follows an external link, overwriting its sentinel even when later rooted rebuild rejects the result. Five before regressions recorded outside repository in /tmp/mpress-s03-conversion-20261002/before.log. Raised to P0 confirmed bug and claimed as required S03 delegate. First checkpoint roots IO and uniquely owns temporary files; broader rollback/config/state/source-delete failure recovery remains required before closure. Preserve explicitly selected CLI conversion directories as separately scoped owned inputs.
Qualified conversion-boundary checkpoint: exact five original HTTP failures at e8eac75 now rejected/preserved; source/state aliases, explicit CLI scope, permissions, ownership and guide-config persistence retained. Full race/vet pass; 100 self/2165 Wails files identical; private unchanged 3 failures/6 assertions. Evidence s03-conversion and S06.md. Per-file atomic commits remain sequential; inject later write/rename/delete/config/state failures and implement/verify complete rollback before closure. P0 IN_PROGRESS.
Boundary checkpoint committed ad9d731 as taliesin-ai. Do not close S06: sequential whole-operation rollback remains required.
WHY / user benefit, 2026-10-26: documentation authors use conversion to change an existing content tree between Markdown and MPD. A later filesystem/configuration failure can leave earlier outputs, deleted originals or updated translation approvals in place because the current commit sequence is not transactional. Benefit: a failed conversion must leave authors with their original usable documents, approval sidecars and configuration instead of manual reconstruction or ambiguous duplicate routes. Evidence so far: current runConversion sequentially publishes targets/sidecars, deletes originals, then saves cfg; ordinary late-failure behavior must be reproduced before claiming a defect fixed. Acceptance for this checkpoint: deterministic target/state/source-delete/config-save failures preserve original bytes/modes/aliases and caller config or retain clearly identified recovery backups if rollback itself fails; successful bidirectional conversion still builds equivalent content and preserves translation metadata. No claim of power-loss durability or unmeasured performance. Investigate first; no refactor solely for code metrics.
2026-10-26 controller review: independent CLI reproduction pinned to main4f807b8 confirms late config-save permission failure deletes original index.md and guide.md while unchanged disk config still points to missing guide. A second clean CLI fixture with page.md and page.markdown confirms duplicate planned target collision: conversion exits0, deletes both originals, emits only the first document. Evidence private conversion-verification/controller-baseline-cli-red.json and controller-baseline-collision-red.json. Existing worker resumed for bounded collision rejection and rollback ownership checks before independent verification. No implementation published yet.
Recovery checkpoint independently reviewed and verified, 2026-10-26: ordinary target-write/source-move/state/config failure restores original bytes, modes, internal aliases and caller configuration; failed rollback reports retained originals. Duplicate exact planned targets rejected before mutations. Controller CLI snapshot/retry MPD strict build/reverse Markdown strict build/collision journeys pass. Full tests/vet, conversion+projectfs+translation+dev race suites and patch golangci-lint pass (0 new issues); Windows conversion test executable cross-compiles, not run. Structural clone heuristics remain reviewed without suppression. Worker continuation completed using technical skills; controller added lexical rename parent-confinement and test portability checks. Evidence private conversion-verification/controller-review.md and controller-*-final.log. Keep S06 IN_PROGRESS: concurrent target promotion, observation/action races, byte-identical replacement ownership and case-insensitive basename collision qualification remain; no crash/power-loss recovery claim. Source publication follows verification; not delivered yet.
DELIVERED checkpoint405bae73786cf2eb2546ae527134f991274fde72 directly to upstream main as verified taliesin-ai, 2026-10-26. Post-push product review at exact published source repeated native CLI late-failure snapshot preservation, successful retry, MPD strict build, reverse Markdown strict build and duplicate-target rejection; all pass. Translation approval migration, failed sidecar rollback, recreated source and generated-target preservation, and retained original recovery-copy journeys pass under race. WHY outcome delivered: ordinary failed conversion leaves authors original usable content and approvals, or names retained originals if restoration cannot complete. No additional confirmed defect in this bounded journey; existing concurrency/case-collision gaps remain on S06, so keep IN_PROGRESS. Next qualification should address exclusive target promotion and precise concurrent-mutation behavior, not repeat the delivered ordinary-error audit. No public docs/rendering change, release or production deployment. Evidence conversion-verification/post-push-cli-journey.json and post-push-product.log; private conceptual research only, no copied code/assets.
WHY for next bounded checkpoint, 2026-10-26: an author or editor can create a new destination document while conversion is running; conversion currently checks existence during enumeration then promotes with replacing rename, so that newly authored file can be silently overwritten. Protect that newly created work. Evidence is a known preflight/promotion gap in published b10e895, still to be demonstrated by a deterministic test before claiming a confirmed fix. Acceptance: inject target creation after planning but before publication, preserve its exact bytes and all original sources, return an actionable collision error and roll back earlier generated outputs; normal bidirectional conversions and sidecar migration retain behavior. Use an atomic no-replace publication primitive, including native case-insensitive filesystem collision handling where available; fail safely if unsupported instead of a check-then-replace fallback. Keep whole-operation concurrency/crash guarantees outside this checkpoint.
Independent baseline proof at b10e895: deterministic real-filesystem timing injection creates b.mpd after enumeration, immediately before original publication; conversion returns nil and replaces newly authored bytes with converted source. Compiled test fails on actual content mismatch, not build/setup failure. Earlier a.mpd also published and originals removed. Evidence private exclusive-verification/controller-baseline-red.log; narrowly confirms destination publication data loss, not an authenticated HTTP exploit or proof about all concurrent mutations.
Exclusive publication checkpoint reviewed/verified, 2026-10-26: newly converted document targets use complete rooted staging and atomic no-replace publication. A destination created after enumeration is preserved byte-for-byte; conversion rejects collision, keeps all original sources and rolls back earlier targets. Existing replacing APIs, sidecar/config behavior and alias boundaries retained. Controller independent baseline actual-content failure and adapted candidate timing test pass red/green. Full tests/vet, projectconvert/projectfs/translate/dev race suites, full patch lint b10e895=0issues pass; Windows projectfs/conversion tests compile only. Controller added published=true-plus-error rollback regression and Windows mode convention fix. Linux strict-build CLI bidirectional conversion/recovery journey passes. Requires file hard-link support; unsupported filesystems fail safely, no replace fallback. Structural helper complexity/clone gates reviewed, not suppressed or called clean. Broader rollback identity/observation-action, sidecar/config concurrency and crash-recovery remain outside this bounded checkpoint. Source publication pending; S06 stays IN_PROGRESS.
DELIVERED exclusive-target publication d9c75e3e4d8bf2e0e92b4a91f31e50507898332a directly to upstream main as verified taliesin-ai. Post-push product review: independent injected new-destination timing test, published-plus-cleanup-error rollback, approved translation migration and complete native CLI failure/retry/bidirectional strict-build journey pass. WHY fulfilled for new destination documents: a document created after planning survives publication refusal intact. No release/deploy. Evidence exclusive-verification/post-push-product.log and post-push-cli-journey.json.
Post-push confirmed remaining P0 finding (deduplicated by conversion issue search): source edits during successful conversion can still be lost. At published d9c75e3, deterministic existing writeNew timing seam modifies page.md after enumeration/read but before actual new-target publication; conversion returns nil, deletes edited page.md and retains an output derived from older bytes. Same compiled scenario adapted to original write seam FAILS identically on baseline b10e895, so this is pre-existing, not a regression introduced by exclusive publication. Expected: detect source change and abort safely with edited source intact and generated outputs rolled back (or retain current edited source as actionable recovery copy), instead of committing stale output and discarding new work. Evidence private exclusive-verification/post-push-source-edit-red.log, baseline-source-edit-red.log and overlay harness; real filesystem data loss under deterministic timing injection, not claimed native concurrent HTTP exploit. Acceptance next: inject real in-place and replacement source edits after planning; preserve edited bytes/mode/link identity as applicable, retain original recovery evidence, return actionable conflict and keep successful unchanged/alias/explicit-directory/translation workflows. Keep S06 P0 IN_PROGRESS; source-version preconditions/guarded removal require further design and tests, not a crash-recovery feature. Do not claim all conversion concurrency fixed.
WHY / user benefit for source-consumption checkpoint, 2026-10-26: authors may keep editing source documents while conversion runs.
